figures.caption: Tē 111 tô.—Oán-sī-gán, kòa phòng-bīn-thàu-kiàⁿ hō͘ kng-sòaⁿ õe chip-sòaⁿ tī bāng-mo̍h-nih. Chit-ê sī in-ūi gán-kiû siuⁿ té, nā bô kòa chit hō thàu-kiàⁿ, sio-tiám õe tī bāng-mo̍h-āu, khòaⁿ bõe bêng (Hartridge).

Tē 112 tô.—Chìⁿ ê siōng chiò tī bák-chiu ê bāng-mo̍h-nih: Tùi chìⁿ-nih kúi nā tiám chhin-chhiūⁿ P, M, H, jit-kng ê sòaⁿ ū chiò-jip bák-chiu-lāi, pîⁿ-chiâⁿ chit ê siōng tī bāng-mo̍h p, m, h; chit ê siōng sī tò-péng khia, iā pí chìⁿ khah sòe. (From “The Household Physician,” Blackie and Son, publisher.)
